It contains no\nwarrior code. The language itself is documented in `redcode/`, `guide.htm` and\n`icws94-standard.txt`.\n\n## Archetypes\n\n- **Imp.** `MOV 0, 1` copies itself one cell ahead forever.\n  - Imps are very hard to kill and kill almost nothing, so on their own they mostly tie.\n  - Several imps spaced CORESIZE/n apart and executed in turn form an *imp ring* or\n    *imp spiral*, which is sturdier.\n- **Stone (bomber).** A small loop that drops bombs (DAT to kill, SPL to slow) at a\n  fixed step through the core.\n  - It is small, fast and hard to find.\n  - The choice of step matters: it decides how evenly and how fast the core gets\n    covered.\n- **Paper (replicator).** Copies itself to new places, again and again, and spawns many\n  processes.\n  - Killing one copy does not kill the warrior, so DAT bombs alone rarely beat it.\n  - \"Silk\" papers copy with `SPL`/`MOV` pairs and post-increment pointers.\n- **Scanner.** Looks for non-empty cells (`SEQ`/`SNE`/`JMZ`), then attacks what it\n  found.\n  - Typical attacks: a few bombs, a carpet of `SPL 0` bombs that stuns the target, or a\n    switch into a core clear.\n  - A scanner has to avoid detecting itself, and its speed is measured in cells per\n    cycle (0.5c, 0.66c, ...).\n- **Core clear.** Overwrites the whole core in sequence, typically with SPL first\n  (stun), then DAT (kill).\n  - Clears are used to finish off stunned opponents. They are often the last phase of a\n    scanner.\n- **Quick-scan (qscan).** A fast, unrolled scan of many cells right at the start of the\n  round.\n  - It catches an opponent before the opponent has booted or replicated.\n  - When it finds nothing, it hands over to the main warrior.\n- **Vampire.** Bombs with `JMP` \"fangs\" that redirect enemy processes into a pit that\n  makes them harmless or useful.\n- **P-space switcher.** Uses the private p-space memory, which persists between the\n  rounds of a battle, to pick a strategy in each round from earlier results. {"type":"text","timestamp":1794659369930,"sessionID":"ses_e25fae85effev8NEIrv8eyezUW","part":{"id":"prt_1da08c3bc0011QbkbTug8BtHXR","messageID":"msg_1da08a494001H5n4kLzbogxvaq","sessionID":"ses_e25fae85effev8NEIrv8eyezUW","type":"text","text":"I submitted \"Folded Silk\", a paper warrior I wrote myself. It scores about **0.42 against the 30 sparring warriors** (300 rounds each). If the hidden hill behaves like the sparring set, that works out to a reward of roughly 0.8, but this is an estimate: I could only test against the sparring warriors, not the hill.\n\n**How it works:**\n- At the start it splits into 16 processes using four `spl 1` lines.\n- Three silk copy stages, with offsets 2364, 4760 and 1308, keep copying the paper to new places in the core.\n- Each copy also drops `dat <2667, <5334` bombs at a 2667 step, which is meant to damage imps and other opponents.\n\n**What I tried that didn't beat it** (sparring scores, 100 rounds each unless noted):\n\n| Variant | Score |\n|---|---|\n| Stone with imp spiral | 0.33 |\n| Two other simple stones | 0.14, 0.06 |\n| My scanners (most likely bugged) | 0.08–0.10 |\n| Quick-scan in front of the paper | 0.37–0.40 |\n| Paper plus imp spiral | 0.405 |\n| Switching between paper and stone after a loss (p-space) | 0.38 |\n| Changing the number of copy stages, the starting processes or the bomb type | 0.34–0.42 |\n| Random copy offsets | 0.38–0.43 |\n\nThe best few versions all landed at 0.419–0.421 over 300 rounds, so the copy offsets hardly matter. That level looks like the limit of this design.\n\n**Weak spots:** it ties a lot, and it clearly loses to a handful of opponents (s01, s06, s17, s21 and s30 score 0.16–0.24), which are probably scanners. A working scanner or a stronger stone, switched in through p-space, would be the next thing to try. I ran out of the 45 minutes before getting either to work.","time":{"start":1794659369916,"end":1794659369928}}}
